title: Evaluation mates and a uniform lower bound for a system right adjoint
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with no separatedness assumption on $Y$, and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, $O=\mathcal O_E$, and let $t\in O$ be nonzero and not a unit [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=O/(t^n)$ for $n\ge1$. Use strict systems $\mathsf S_A(W_{\mathrm{et}})$, evaluation $e_n$, and their ordinary unbounded derived categories as in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Set $F_A=Rp_{f,A,*}j_{!,A}$ and $F_n=Rp_{f,*,A_n}j_!$. 
Fix an adjunction $F_A\dashv G_A$ on the unbounded derived categories. Assume the canonical evaluation and derived-left-extension identifications $e_nF_A\cong F_ne_n$ and $F_AL_n\cong L_nF_n$ of [lem-pur-etale-system-brown-construction]. Fix finite-level adjunctions $F_n\dashv g_n$ with units $\eta_n$ and counits $\epsilon_n$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Then there is a natural isomorphism $\theta_n:e_nG_A\cong g_ne_n$, uniquely specified by the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(P,e_nG_AM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_nP,G_AM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_AL_nP,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_nF_nP,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_nP,e_nM)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,g_ne_nM).$$
It identifies the evaluated counit with $\epsilon_n$ and the evaluated unit with $\eta_n$, using $e_nF_A\cong F_ne_n$ in the latter equation.

For $m\ge n$ write $T^W_{m,n}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$, $q_{m,n}:T^Y_{m,n}F_m\cong F_nT^X_{m,n}$ for the coefficient projection, and let $b_{m,n}:T^X_{m,n}g_m\to g_nT^Y_{m,n}$ be the $F_n\dashv g_n$ transpose of $T^Y_{m,n}\epsilon_m\circ q_{m,n,g_m}^{-1}$. Under the $\theta_n$, the adjoint transition of $G_AM$ is
$$T^X_{m,n}g_mM_m\xrightarrow{b_{m,n}}g_nT^Y_{m,n}M_m\xrightarrow{g_n(t^M_{m,n})}g_nM_n.$$
This identifies actual transition maps, compatibly with three indices, rather than just evaluated objects.

Suppose $N\ge0$ satisfies $F_n(D^{\le b})\subset D^{\le b+N}$ for every integer $b$ and every $n$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. Then $G_A(D^{\ge a})\subset D^{\ge a-N}$ for every integer $a$, with the same $N$.

proof.text: Transpose the coefficient mate identity and composition assertions through the finite adjunctions. The coefficient projection unit and cocycle, naturality, and the mate counit equation identify both words. Independently derive the scalar-adjoint transition identity and composition for any system from P.mate, sigma_id and sigma_comp. Combine these equations with the actual transition formula and cancel the evaluation isomorphisms to obtain the right-system identity and composition.

proof.text: For M in degree at least a, B.componentsY.bounds gives the same bound on every evaluation. If P is at most a-N-1, the assumed amplitude puts F_n P at most a-1, so every map F_n P to e_n M is zero by t-structure orthogonality. The finite adjunction therefore makes every map P to g_n e_n M zero. Mathlib isGE_iff_orthogonal gives g_n e_n M in degree at least a-N directly. Transport this bound through theta and use B.componentsX.bounds to conclude for G M, with the original N.
